plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding exactly my value of $31 maximizes my expected profit - I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay less than my value, and I don't want to risk winning at a price above my value or losing a profitable opportunity. No history exists to suggest deviation from this optimal strategy.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value, since bidding higher risks overpaying relative to my value, and bidding lower only reduces my chance of winning without improving the price I'd pay. With no prior history to adjust for opponent behavior, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where I pay the second-highest bid if I win. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $40.
